label: Expandable Checkbox
title: Expandable Checkbox
summary: Use an Expandable Checkbox for one consent whose text is too long for a line, such as agreeing to share KYC details.
corePrinciple: Ticking gives consent; Read more only shows the words.

anatomy.title: A checkbox row with its own toggle
anatomy.description: The checkbox item holds the box, the consent label, and an optional link to the document. Read more sits at the end of the row and only opens or closes the text.

sizing.title: Full width, 24 px when Idle

content.title: A consent phrase, the document, and plain toggles
content.description: Start the label with the consent, in sentence case without a full stop. Name the document in the link. Rename the toggles only in pairs, and keep them short, such as “Show terms” and “Hide terms”.

inContext.title: Consent before opening an account
inContext.description: One row per agreement. The screen keeps each row’s checked state and enables Open account only after the required consent; each row opens and closes on its own.

sources.title: Use the public Expandable Checkbox contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Expandable Checkbox has two states, Idle and Open; checked, disabled, the number of collapsed lines, and the toggle labels exist only in the package. Figma and the package both set the label in regular weight. On the web the row is one checkbox that announces whether it is ticked, Read more announces whether the text is open, and Enter or Space ticks or unticks the box once. The Terms link opens with the keyboard, and an open sentence wraps inside the row.
